result:
I've written all four sample apps, the shell-side preview wiring and the design notes. Nothing has been tested: I had no shell access, so no browser, build or test ran, and I'm not claiming any visual check.

**What each app keeps from its real source:**
- **Wisdom** uses the exact `--serif` stack throughout, so reading stays large and serif. It keeps the editorial library (poster covers, shelves, search, library tabs, Browse grid), the collection page, and the full-page reader that turns pages like the real app. It opens on a reading of *Meditations* (George Long's public-domain translation); Back goes to the library.
- **Music** keeps the search bar, artwork shelf, track lists, the persistent mini player and the full-screen Now Playing. The 12 records are invented and their covers are drawn in CSS. The player only moves a local clock: no audio, no network.
- **Signal** keeps the dense timeline: tabs, filters, post rows with signal-depth markers, sources, settings, bottom nav and the add-source sheet. I added a post detail view (tap a post) and a channel view (tap a name), both built from the same row markup.
- **Topics** keeps the Today/Following/Archive panes, editions and cards, and the topic, report (with sample deep dives), day and follow sheets.
- **Colour modes:** "unified" and "original" render the same markup, fonts and sizes; only the palette changes. Anything printed on photos, plus album art and status colours, stays the same in both. All sample content is labelled as sample in place, and anything that can't work is either left out or shown disabled as "sample only".

**Back button:** each app's `window.__wizardCloseOverlay()` returns true only when it actually closed something or left a nested view, and false at the app's root. Every such step also changes something the shell's 180 ms check reads (a heading, a dialog, or a "Back to…" label), so the shell won't take a second step on top. Inside the shell the apps add no history entries at boot. Opened directly in a browser tab, the first Back at root shows "Press back again to exit" and stays.

**Candidate index:**
- `core/shell.js`, `core/tour.js` and the PWA install script are not loaded. Everything in `core/*` and `app.js` is untouched.
- `demo/preview-boot.js` runs first. It keeps the phone shell at any width and pre-fills the app list with the four sample apps. It lays out the desks as Home, Wisdom (in front), Music, Signal, Topics, and marks the tour done.
- The preview blocks every request that isn't a GET or HEAD, `sendBeacon`, and microphone access. So the orb can't record, and anything you type or say to send will show up as failed in the outbox.
- The Preview pill opens a small sheet. It has the six skins (via `WosSkin.set`), Unified/Original, and shortcuts to the four apps and Architecture. Comparison and open are sent as the cancelable `wizard:comparison` and `wizard:open` events. If nothing claims them, the controls fall back to the shell's own routes (`?open=` and `__wos.openLinkDesk`), so the page never navigates away.

**Known issues to check in the rendered review:**
- **Apps paint their own background.** This overrides `ui.css`'s transparent window mode for these four apps only. The shell paints a fixed near-black behind each app frame, so a transparent page would put the Paper skin's dark text on near-black. You may want to fix this in `ui.css` instead.
- **Small Preview pill.** Its touch area is about 17 px tall so it never reaches the window title bars. The controls inside the sheet are 44 px.
- **Shared storage.** If the preview is served from the same origin as production, it shares the desk layout and app list keys with it. I copy the existing layout to `wos.preview.backup` first, and `WosPreview.restore()` puts it back, but a separate origin would be safer.
- **Back with the sheet open:** on browsers without CloseWatcher, one Back closes the Preview sheet and also takes a shell step.
- `demo/architecture.html` belongs to you. Until it exists, the Architecture shortcut opens a 404.
- Small departures from the source: Wisdom's rating button is renamed `.wb-thumb-btn` because `.wb-thumb` clashes with the row thumbnails, and a few Topics controls got a larger minimum height for touch.

The notes also include the full colour mapping table and the reasoning behind the comparison mode.

Files are in `web/demo/apps/` and `web/demo/`, plus the edits to `web/index.html` and `docs/evidence/`:
- `wisdom.html`, `wisdom.css`, `wisdom.js`
- `music.html`, `music.css`, `music.js`
- `signal.html`, `signal.css`, `signal.js`
- `topics.html`, `topics.css`, `topics.js`
- `shared/fixture.js`
- `preview-boot.js`
- `preview-controls.css`, `preview-controls.js`
- `web/index.html`
- `web/data.js`, `web/summaries.js` (empty, and gitignored)
- `opus-design-notes.md`
